Re-vendor:  bash Scripts/vendor_musashi.sh (fetches the pinned commit, verifies the SHA, copies the
            upstream files, applies the 1-line m68kconf.h change, regenerates m68kops.c/.h and
            checks their sha1, and checks that the MX68K stubs exist and the excluded upstream
            files are absent). The script never touches the MX68K-authored files listed below.

  MX68K-authored port (1) — NOT an upstream Musashi file (contains the marker
  "MX68K作成の移植版(MAME m68kfpu.cpp 由来"), P897:
    m68kfpu.c              MX68K-authored port of MAME src/devices/cpu/m68000/m68kfpu.cpp
                           (BSD-3-Clause, Karl Stenerud/R. Belmont,
                           pinned 4ae561d0019312c0af7a519c2d22f52968e029e1), rewritten in C for the
                           Musashi CPU struct/macros; the BSD-3 notice is kept at the top of the file.
                           The instruction decoding inside m68040_fpu_op0/op1 (040fpu0/040fpu1) was
                           written by MX68K from the instruction formats; MAME's m68k_in.lst (no license
                           notice) was consulted only as a reference, not used as a source.
                           Arithmetic and transcendental functions go to ThirdParty/softfloat_2a
                           (Hatari, SoftFloat 2a; transcendental functions from softfloat_fpsp.c).
                           FMOVE.P (packed decimal) is not supported (line-1111).
                           FSAVE/FRESTORE frames follow the selected chip (68881 IDLE 28B / 68882 IDLE
                           60B, Motorola MC68881/MC68882 User's Manual 1st ed. 1987).
                           FPU present only with MX68K_MUSASHI_FPU=1 on EC030 (Bridge/mx_cpu_musashi.c);
                           otherwise F2xx/F3xx take the line-1111 exception exactly as the former P869
                           stub, including the observation hook mx68k_musashi_stub_hook (defined here,
                           NULL by default). #included by m68kcpu.c; not compiled on its own.
                           FDBcc/FTRAPcc/FScc abs ($F248-$F24F, $F278-$F27F): m68ki_build_opcode_table()
                           lets cpdbcc/cptrapcc overwrite those 040fpu0 table entries; since P899 the
                           Bridge restores them at startup (see "Runtime jump-table changes" below).
  MX68K-authored stubs (2) — NOT upstream files (each contains the marker "MX68K作成のスタブ"):
    m68kmmu.h              m68881_mmu_ops: PMMU general form ($F000-$F03F) with EA Dn/(An) -> no-op
                           (reads the 2nd word only; EC030 has no MMU, as XEiJ irpPgen), every other
                           form -> line-1111 exception; both notify mx68k_musashi_stub_hook (P869).
                           pmmu_translate_addr -> abort() (unreachable: nothing sets PMMU_ENABLED).
                           Hook kind values (1=fpu_fline, 2=pmmu_noop, 3=pmmu_fline) must match
                           m68kfpu.c / m68kmmu.h / Bridge/mx_cpu_musashi.c.
    softfloat/milieu.h     type definitions only (int8..sbits64, used by upstream Musashi; `flag` is no
                           longer defined here since P897 — softfloat_2a's softfloat.h defines it).
  MX68K-authored shim (1) (contains the marker "MX68K作成の転送shim"), P897:
    softfloat/softfloat.h  1-line forwarding shim to ../../softfloat_2a/softfloat.h (types for the CPU
                           struct's floatx80 fpr[8] and the softfloat_2a API used by m68kfpu.c).
  MX68K-authored (1): this MX68K_VENDOR.txt.

Excluded (not vendored) and why:
  - softfloat/ (upstream softfloat.c, softfloat.h, milieu.h, softfloat-macros,
    softfloat-specialize, mamesf.h): SoftFloat Release 2b carries an indemnification clause.
    Only the original m68kfpu.c calls into it, and that file is not vendored either.
  - m68kfpu.c (upstream): no license notice.
  - m68kmmu.h (upstream): legacy MAME license notice.
  - example/, test/, Makefile, .gitignore. (test/ is fetched temporarily by
    Scripts/musashi_selftest.sh from the same pinned commit.)
  Current state (P896/P897): the FPU now uses SoftFloat 2a via ThirdParty/softfloat_2a (Hatari),
  vendored separately; no SoftFloat 2b code is included anywhere. The upstream m68kfpu.c is still
  not vendored — ThirdParty/Musashi/m68kfpu.c is the MX68K-authored MAME-derived port above.
  With the 68000 CPU type the stubs are unreachable: FPU opcodes take the line-1111 exception
  (CPU_TYPE_IS_030_PLUS check in m68k_in.c), and PMMU is disabled (has_pmmu=0).
  The stubs are reached only by the experimental EC030 models (MX68K_MUSASHI_MODEL=ec030 /
  ec030-bare, with MX68K_CPU_CORE=musashi; P869). ec030 sets has_pmmu=1 on the EC030 type so that
  PMMU opcodes reach m68kmmu.h; side effect: the upstream 68040 "pflush" handler ($F518) then
  becomes a silent no-op (prints "68040: unhandled PFLUSH" to stderr) instead of line-1111.

Runtime jump-table changes (P899, D-84) — the files above stay unmodified, but the Bridge changes
Musashi's runtime behaviour, so it is recorded here:
  - Where: Bridge/mx_cpu_musashi.c mx_musashi_fix_cp_dispatch(), called once from
    mx_cpu_musashi_init() right after m68k_init() (the table is built only there).
  - What: upstream's generic coprocessor handlers (cpgen/cpscc/cpdbcc/cptrapcc/cpbcc) return
    silently on EC020+ regardless of cpID ("unemulated" placeholders). The Bridge rewrites
    (a) every cpID 2-7 entry that points to one of those 5 handlers -> m68k_op_1111 (line-1111),
        expected 1528 entries (move16 $F620-$F627 etc. are left alone: matched by pointer);
    (b) cpID 1 $F248-$F24F / $F278-$F27F (cpdbcc/cptrapcc) -> 040fpu0, expected 16 entries,
        also copying m68ki_cycles[*][0xF200] into those entries.
    cpID 0 (PMMU, $F000-$F1FF) is not changed.
  - Why: a real MC68030 takes the F-line exception when the coprocessor is absent
    (MC68030 UM §8.1.5 / §10.5.2.2); Human68k FPACK ($FExx) relies on it.
  - Re-vendor check: the startup log line "[P899-CPFIX] fline=1528 fpu=16 cpdup=0" (or an
    "[P899-CPFIX] ABORT reason=..." line) shows whether the table layout still matches. If a new
    upstream changes NUM_CPU_TYPES (m68kops.c), update MX_MUSASHI_NUM_CPU_TYPES in the Bridge too.

Notes for 68030 support (to do in that cycle):
  - P869 implemented the minimal EC030 + no-FPU stubs above; P897 replaced the FPU stub with the
    MAME-derived port (environment-variable gated). Not implemented: PMMU no-op for the remaining EA
    modes (An/(An)+/-(An)/d16/d8/abs/PC-relative/#imm), a real PMMU.
  - Replace the PMMU stub with a real implementation (re-check provenance/licensing of the
    upstream m68kmmu.h, or write new code) — abort() is only acceptable while unreachable.
  - Narrow the M68K_EMULATE_* options to what MX68K actually needs.

Build notes (MX68K):
  - m68kcpu.c and m68kops.c are compiled into both targets (MX68K and MX68K-iOS),
    COMPILER_FLAGS = -w (upstream warnings). Bridge/mx_cpu_musashi.c is compiled without -w.
  - No .h file from ThirdParty/Musashi is added to the Xcode project, and ThirdParty/Musashi is
    NOT in HEADER_SEARCH_PATHS: a bare "m68k.h" would resolve through the Xcode header map to
    the unrelated legacy stub in Core/px68k/m68000/Musashi/. Include Musashi headers from
    Bridge/ by relative path only ("../ThirdParty/Musashi/m68kcpu.h"); mx_cpu_musashi.c has
    compile-time guards that fail the build on a wrong resolution.
  - m68kfpu.c, m68kdasm.c, m68kmake.c and m68k_in.c are not compiled by Xcode.
